context:
Morrow Works is a fictional purchasing cooperative. Its master record is a legal vendor organization, not a contact person, branch, brand, or parent group. Three source systems provide 620,000 vendor rows. The current pipeline blocks on country and a normalized name prefix, scores candidate pairs using names, addresses and identifiers, admits edges above 0.92, then applies connected components. Branches sometimes share a registered address; some procurement identifiers represent payment groups rather than legal entities. Their namespace and validity dates are not yet audited.

The largest component contains 4,200 rows. Analysts found several low-margin bridges and a high-degree shared address node. On 300 convenience-sampled pairs within that component, the scorer looked accurate, but this sample was not designed to estimate entity precision. The business wants to “fix graph clustering” without changing scoring, while a developer proposes raising the edge threshold. A bad merge can route a payment to the wrong payee. Auditors require a reversible explanation of membership changes; there is no authorization to alter payment records. Staff can examine 40 proposed component splits this month.

Write a bounded diagnosis and experiment plan. Distinguish changing admitted evidence from changing resolution on fixed edges; compare a simple baseline with an alternative. Explain where closure, contradictory evidence and constraints matter, which observations are merely topology diagnostics, and how to evaluate entity-level harm without treating absent edges as confirmed negatives. Identify prerequisites, stopping conditions and the next reversible action.
title: Morrow Works vendor graph
